This is a follow-up revision within the same correction-mode pass on spec_file_path=/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/specs/SPEC-002-native-artifact-placement.json (criterion_id=AC-008 was already corrected in the prior round; that correction was verified accurate by exit-gate and must NOT be changed further).

Read the full spec JSON from that path yourself. Read /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/ARCHITECTURE.md lines 440-513 (the §12 example workflow, including the comment annotation around lines 507-509) yourself to verify ground truth.

canon:gate-spec just ran on the AC-008-corrected spec and returned verdict FAIL, with one blocker (not on AC-008, which it verified as accurate) — on AC-009:

---
Blocker on AC-009 (criterion at .claude/specs/SPEC-002-native-artifact-placement.json:74; target under test at ARCHITECTURE.md:474-513):

AC-009 requires ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example to "show" three things, one of which is "a placement step downloading that artifact into its package directory". Two defects:
(1) Untestable: "read end to end, shows" is a human reading judgment with no mechanical predicate, unlike its siblings AC-007 and AC-008, which specify greppable string conditions.
(2) Contradicts sibling criteria: AC-010 requires that a consumer add "no additional bash, composite action, or script authored by the consumer to perform placement", and AC-011 requires §6.2 to gain a note saying callisto-action performs placement automatically in-step. An implementer following AC-009's plain reading would add a literal `gh run download` step to §12's example and thereby violate the pattern AC-010 and AC-011 establish. The example at ARCHITECTURE.md:507-509 currently represents placement only as a YAML comment above the callisto-action step, and AC-009 does not determine whether that satisfies it.

Required change: replace AC-009's text with a mechanically checkable version that names the comment-annotation form as the correct one, e.g. "ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow code block contains all three of: (a) a job with an actions/upload-artifact step whose `name` input is `${{ matrix.target.artifactName }}`; (b) a subsequent job that invokes `./.github/actions/callisto-action` with `publish: true`; and (c) a comment line immediately preceding that callisto-action step stating that artifact placement into each packageDir happens automatically inside the action once nativeMatrix is non-empty and publish is enabled. The block contains no consumer-authored `gh run download` invocation, consistent with AC-010 and AC-011." If the intent is instead that the example must show a literal placement step, then AC-010 and AC-011 must be revised in the same pass and the conflict resolved explicitly; do not leave both readings available.
---

Task:
1. Read ARCHITECTURE.md lines 440-513 yourself and confirm exactly what's there (exact upload-artifact step `name` field, exact callisto-action invocation, exact comment text if any) before rewriting AC-009 — do not just copy the gate's suggested wording verbatim if the actual file differs in some detail; ground the rewrite in what you actually observe.
2. Rewrite AC-009 to be mechanically checkable (greppable/observable conditions, not a human reading judgment) and consistent with AC-010 and AC-011's "consumer writes no placement code, callisto-action does it automatically" model. Do not touch AC-008 (already correct) or any other criterion unless you find a genuine matching inconsistency — if so, revise it and explain why in reasoning.
3. Return the COMPLETE spec@1 object (all fields: id, purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface, all 11 acceptance_criteria, linked_requirement, revision_note, reasoning). Update revision_note to describe BOTH the original AC-008 correction (bare matrix.hostRunner -> namespaced matrix.target.<field>, per lambda:exit-gate's contradiction report) AND this AC-009 correction (untestable/contradictory language -> mechanically checkable form, per canon:gate-spec's blocker), citing both criterion ids and both reasons.
4. Do not set spec_file_path in your output.

Output the full corrected spec@1 JSON as your final message.

> **Status: napi-rs and maturin platform-target discovery, plus npm/PyPI runtime-version constraints, are implemented** (`callisto matrix [--package <name>]`, `--format text|json` via the global flag). Java (JNI) target discovery, .NET native-AOT target discovery, and the `callisto publish-target` subcommand described later in this section remain unimplemented and are planned for a future release.

To eliminate configuration duplication and configuration drift across native Rust, NAPI-RS, Maturin (Python), and Java (JNI) polyglot monorepos, `callisto matrix` provides dynamic matrix auto-discovery:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               CALLISTO NATIVE MATRIX AUTO-DISCOVERY                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Workspace Manifests (Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml)        │
│ ↳ Single Source of Truth: napi.targets, maturin.targets, engines.node  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ callisto matrix --format json                                          │
│ ↳ Dynamically computes runner OS, target triples, & runtime versions   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ GitHub Actions / GitLab CI Job Matrix                                  │
│ ↳ Parallel native build matrix execution without hardcoded YAML arrays  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Manifest-Driven Target Auto-Detection

1. **NAPI-RS (`package.json`)**: Auto-detects `napi.targets` (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and maps them to a GitHub Actions runner label per triple (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`/`macos-13`, `windows-latest`, plus `cross`-gated Linux/Android/FreeBSD targets).
2. **Maturin (`pyproject.toml`)**: Auto-detects `tool.maturin.targets` and Python runtime compatibility bounds.
3. **Runtime Engine Compatibility**: Automatically extracts Node.js (`engines.node`) and Python (`requires-python`) version ranges directly from package manifests, eliminating duplicate version strings in CI YAML. Java (`java.version`/`pom.xml`) extraction is not yet implemented, consistent with this section's status note above.

### Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern

```yaml
jobs:
  matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      nativeMatrix: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.nativeMatrix }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - id: discover
        run: echo "nativeMatrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build:
    needs: matrix
    if: ${{ needs.matrix.outputs.nativeMatrix != '[]' }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        target: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix.outputs.nativeMatrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.target.hostRunner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto
      - run: napi build --platform --release --target ${{ matrix.target.triple }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.target.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ matrix.target.packageDir }}/*.node

  release:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Placement of each build job's uploaded artifact into its packageDir,
      # then callisto publish, both happen automatically inside this step
      # once nativeMatrix is non-empty and publish is enabled.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          publish: true
```

2	  "id": "SPEC-002",
3	  "purpose": "Give callisto consumers a working, documented mechanism that places CI-built native binary artifacts (napi-rs .node files, maturin wheels) into their platform-stub package directories before `callisto publish` runs, closing the gap between `callisto matrix`'s output and a working end-to-end release, with artifact names that stay unique when multiple packages in one workspace share a target triple.",
4	  "scope": "Two changes. (1) Rust: `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs`'s `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String` is replaced with `artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name: &str, triple: &str) -> String`, returning `format!(\"native-{package_name}-{triple}\")`; `build_platform_target` (already receiving `package_name` as a parameter) is updated to call it. This embeds the already-workspace-unique `package_name` (a value `PlatformTarget` already carries, sourced from each package's own identity) into `artifactName`, so two different packages declaring the same triple no longer produce colliding CI artifact names. (2) GitHub Actions: extends `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite-action step -- within the block already guarded by `[[ -n \"$INPUT_PUBLISH\" && \"$INPUT_PUBLISH\" != \"false\" ]]` (action.yml:167), immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed, adds a placement loop that downloads each `nativeMatrix` entry's artifact by `artifactName` (pinned to the current run via `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`) and places its contents into `packageDir`. Also updates `.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md` §6.2 and corrects `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12's broken example workflow.",
5	  "non_goals": [
6	    "Extending PlatformTargetKind to Java/JNI or .NET native-AOT targets -- a separate, later concern; this spec only routes the two kinds PlatformTargetKind already supports (Napi, Maturin).",
7	    "Prebuilt Rust CLI binaries distributed as GitHub Release assets (\"Tier 2\") -- a separate, related, deferred future spec.",
8	    "Homebrew tap formula generation/distribution -- deferred by the maintainer as a possible separate future tool.",
9	    "Go binary distribution -- already an existing non-goal per .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §8, not being revisited here.",
10	    "A generic callisto-build-action that dispatches the actual per-platform build (napi build --platform --release, etc.) -- callisto-matrix.md §7's secondary/optional proposal. This spec covers only placement of an already-built, correctly-named artifact; the build step itself is the consumer's own responsibility.",
11	    "Validating the content of a downloaded artifact (e.g. confirming a .node file is well-formed, or that it is actually a valid binary for its target triple). The placement step moves whatever files gh run download retrieves into packageDir; content correctness is the build job's responsibility and surfaces later, at publish or install time, not at placement.",
12	    "Adding a new required input to callisto-action to opt into placement. Placement is driven entirely by whether nativeMatrix is a non-empty array -- consumers with no native platform targets see zero behavior change.",
13	    "Implementing the nonexistent callisto publish-target Rust CLI subcommand referenced by ARCHITECTURE.md §12's status note (line 447). That subcommand is not needed for this requirement and is not built by this spec; the status note's reference to it (alongside Java/.NET native-AOT discovery) remains accurate and is deliberately left in place -- only the example workflow's own code block, which currently invokes the nonexistent subcommand directly and dereferences nonexistent matrix.os/matrix.package/matrix.target-as-scalar fields, is corrected.",
14	    "Guaranteeing that a binary placed at packageDir by this step is picked up and included in callisto publish's registry upload output (npm tarball, PyPI wheel, etc.). That round-trip guarantee is owned by whatever spec governs callisto publish's own native-binary packaging logic (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs) -- this spec's guarantee ends at the file being present on disk at packageDir before publish begins.",
15	    "Handling malformed or invalid-JSON nativeMatrix values within callisto-action's own in-step placement loop. NATIVE_MATRIX (action.yml:164) is produced and consumed entirely within one shell step under `set -o pipefail`, with `jq` already validating JSON syntax (and failing the step via `|| { echo \"::error::callisto matrix failed\"; exit 1; }`) before the placement loop added by this spec ever reads the value -- malformed JSON cannot reach this specific loop by construction. This does not apply to a consumer's own custom multi-job pipeline built against callisto-matrix.md §6.2's standalone reference snippet, where nativeMatrix genuinely crosses a job-output boundary; that snippet's own error handling is out of scope for this spec beyond the run-id pin AC-011 requires.",
16	    "Handling a missing (absent-key) or null artifactName/packageDir field on an otherwise-valid nativeMatrix entry. crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs's PlatformTarget declares both fields as plain `String` (not `Option<String>`), so serde can never serialize a missing or null value for either field into the JSON callisto matrix emits.",
17	    "Preserving the exact literal string format `native-{triple}` (no package-name component) as a stable, versioned contract of callisto matrix's JSON output. This spec deliberately changes artifactName's value (adding a package_name segment) to fix the collision defect; a consumer that hardcoded the old two-segment format rather than treating artifactName as an opaque per-entry correlation token (its documented purpose) will observe a different string. No config override for this naming scheme is provided -- package_name is already sourced from the package's own identity, which is already user-configurable through the normal manifest name field; a separate artifact-naming override would duplicate that control for no benefit, since the artifact name is a CI-internal correlation id, never published or user-facing."
18	  ],
19	  "api_surface": [
20	    {
21	      "name": "artifact_name_for_package_triple",
22	      "signature": "pub(crate) fn artifact_name_for_package_triple(package_name: &str, triple: &str) -> String",
23	      "description": "Replaces `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String`. Returns `format!(\"native-{package_name}-{triple}\")`. `build_platform_target` (crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:126-142), which already receives `package_name` as its third parameter, calls this instead of the old triple-only function when constructing `PlatformTarget.artifact_name`."
24	    },
25	    {
26	      "name": "callisto-action native artifact placement loop",
27	      "signature": "New shell logic inside `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite step, placed inside the `[[ -n \"$INPUT_PUBLISH\" && \"$INPUT_PUBLISH\" != \"false\" ]]` guard (action.yml:167) immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed (action.yml:164-165) and before `callisto plan-publish`/publish executes.",
28	      "description": "Feeds `NATIVE_MATRIX` through process substitution, not a pipe -- `while IFS= read -r ENTRY; do ... done < <(printf '%s' \"$NATIVE_MATRIX\" | jq -c '.[]')` -- matching the existing pattern used for the releases loop at action.yml:219, so an `exit 1` inside the loop body terminates the step itself, not a subshell.
